title: Bloomberg links project wallet to Melania Trump NFT’s roughly $185,000 winning bid
description_short: Bloomberg links project wallet to Melania Trump NFT’s roughly $185,000 winning bid
description_medium: Bloomberg examined the January 2022 auction of Melania Trump’s “Head of State” NFT and traced cryptocurrency transfers from a wallet linked to the project to the wallet that placed the 1,800-SOL winning bid, then valued at about $185,000. The report concerns one auction transaction, not total collection revenue, and the wallet trail alone does not establish who controlled each wallet.
description_long: Melania Trump’s “Head of State” NFT was auctioned in January 2022. Bloomberg’s February 16 report examined blockchain transactions and traced a series of transfers from a wallet associated with the project to the wallet that placed the winning bid. The bid was 1,800 SOL, worth about $185,000 at the time. Those figures describe one winning transaction: SOL is the cryptocurrency amount, while the dollar amount is its approximate contemporaneous value, not an additional payment or a collection-wide sales total. Bloomberg raised questions about the source of the bid, but the reported wallet connection does not by itself identify the people controlling either wallet or establish their intent. The article does not substantiate the claim that Melania’s collection earned more than $45 million, show that taxpayers funded the purchase, or document later Trump-family NFT sales. The evidence supports an attributed account of one auction and a wallet trail, not a total-revenue or government-funding conclusion.

supported_facts: Bloomberg reports the January 2022 auction of Melania Trump’s “Head of State” NFT.
The winning bid was 1,800 SOL, worth approximately $185,000 at the time; these express one transaction in cryptocurrency and its approximate contemporaneous dollar value.
Bloomberg traces transfers from a wallet associated with the project toward the wallet that placed the winning bid.
limits: The report concerns one auction/bid and does not establish total collection revenue or later Trump-family NFT sales.
A wallet link/transfer trail does not conclusively identify wallet controllers, establish intent, or demonstrate taxpayer funding.

unsupported_original_claims: The collection earned more than $45 million in January 2022.
The cited investigation establishes wallet beneficial ownership or intent.
The cited report establishes later Trump-family NFT sales totals.
exact_evidence_gap: The Bloomberg report supports one 1,800-SOL bid and a reported wallet-transfer link. It does not establish overall collection revenue, who controlled the wallets, why transfers occurred, taxpayer funding, or later family NFT sales.
